proposedOverrides.summary: An epigraphically attested Satavahana district name that the atlas expands into an oversized 1 BCE to 500 CE polity, with dynasty, province and later regional continuity carefully separated.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact target satavahanihara is indexed approximately 1 BCE to 500 CE, with label Satavahanihara and alias Satava.; it was missing a card and override at initial audit.
Satavahanihara is an epigraphically grounded territorial name related to Satavahana ahara, or district, and is not treated as a synonym for the entire Satavahana dynasty.
At 1 BCE, 100, 200 and 300 the target is the same one-part, one-ring, 51-position Polygon with SHA-256 3da3734817b8ece4c666ceffc6f5c91514af3339b827a2a388917e5db7bddfa4.

The repeated target includes Tagara, Nagardhan, Sannati, Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda, Kondapur and Kotalingala, but excludes Paithan, Nashik, Naneghat, Junnar, Karle, Kanheri, Sopara, Bharuch, Ujjain, Vidisha, Ajanta and Kanchipuram.
The atlas assigns much of the excluded western Satavahana core to saka-kingdom through 300. At 400 the target shrinks to 21 positions and Gupta takes western centers and Amaravati.
At 500 the target disappears; Vakataka, Gupta and Pallava polygons divide tested places. These are separately indexed and carded identities, not authorized aliases or one-to-one successors.
No appliesTo mapping is added. The override keeps atlas dateBasis, leaves fell null and has no successor ids because the exact district label has no documented single conquest or direct heir.
